about: Vectors for mpp/charge/usdc/gateway. Expected values were computed with canonicalize 5.1.0 and viem keccak256, canonicalize and js-sha3, and Python json.dumps with eth-utils keccak, which agreed. The TransferSpec runs from Arc Testnet (domain 26) to Base Sepolia (domain 6), the testnet wallet and minter of gateway-api-testnet.circle.com /v1/info, each address left-padded to 32 bytes. The payer key is the published Anvil development key #0; the signature is made at test time and is not verified by bound. The ceiling section's oracles: Circle's Gateway API reference for GET /v1/info (developers.circle.com/api-reference/gateway/all/get-gateway-info, read 2026-11-17), which serves burnIntentExpirationHeight per network as a decimal string, the current minimum accepted burn intent expiration height; Circle's Gateway technical guide (developers.circle.com/gateway/references/technical-guide, read 2026-11-17), under which Gateway takes a transfer request only while its maxBlockHeight is at least the wallet's withdrawalDelay above the source chain's current block; and Circle's own client, @circle-fin/x402-batching 4.0.0 (this workspace's pinned devDependency), whose GatewayClient reads withdrawalDelay as the Gateway Wallet's uint256 view withdrawalDelay() (dist/client/index.mjs:763-769, :1642-1647) and whose createBurnIntent (dist/client/index.mjs:1472-1495) signs maxBlockHeight 2^256 - 1, run at test time on Arc Testnet to Base Sepolia with the payer key above, which gives M5's spec but for its random salt. Each expectMaxBlockHeight is burnIntentExpirationHeight + ceil(withdrawalDelay x 100 / 604800), computed with Python 3.12.3 integer arithmetic, h + -(-d * 100 // 604800), refused where it exceeds 2^256 - 1. The heights and delays are chosen to exercise the arithmetic and were not read from a network.

M5.case: usdcRequestHash of R_G, usdcGatewaySalt, the credential's bound and its refusals. complete wraps the buyer's signed burn intent in the Gateway Transfer credential the usdc draft writes (draft-usdc-charge-00, blob ec7fc1868b, L615-636 and the A.4 example L1304-1349): challenge, source, then payload {type "transfer", sourceNetwork, destinationNetwork, maxFee, authorization {format "circle-gateway-v1", transfer {burnIntent, signature}}}; payload is that object written by hand in the draft's member order, with the signature made at test time

pattern.proves: The payer signed a Circle Gateway burn intent whose TransferSpec salt is keccak256 of the JCS of this challenge's id and parameters, and the id is this ATR's hash in base64url with the challenge's position. The signature is not verified here. The salt travels inside the TransferSpec that the destination mint carries, and the Gateway Minter emits that TransferSpec's keccak256 hash; this record reads no chain, and settlement is the seller's report. This does not show that amount, payee, asset or timing match the ATR's content.

buyer.about: The buyer gate's rows for this file's pairings, in the form of buyer.json's rows. B2 is the plant: the document advertises H, the hash of the ATR in B6's first check, and the link serves the planted ATR, that ATR with one byte changed; the gate declines hash-mismatch and never calls the signer. B6 is the pairing's bound check over the payment this file already holds: check(ATR, presented) gives H, and check(planted ATR, presented) declines signed-not-bound. Where the ATR is abc, H is its SHA-256 (FIPS 180-2 B.1) and the planted ATR is abd. SHA-256 values are GNU coreutils sha256sum, which openssl dgst -sha256 matches. Bytes are hex. A B2 input names the account, the buyer's inputs and the time (now, in seconds) its build needs. noSignedPayment names each pairing of the file that has no B6 row, and why.

rows.name: B6
rows.note: presented is the payment built from fixed.payerKey and M5's payload: its burn intent's EIP-712 domain separator is M5.expectDomainSeparator and its digest has M5.expectDigest's prefix and suffix, and its signature is the payer key's RFC 6979 signature of that digest.

boundChallenge.case: The file's credential at `credential`, a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into this file, presented with its echoed challenge replaced by `challenge`, the same challenge with the change the row's case names: pairingsOf, over the challenge as issued, does not name `pairing` for it, and that pairing's bound and reference refuse the credential with the row's code, the code pairingsOf gives (mpp/not-this-pairing where it names other pairings). The request is base64url, without padding, of its RFC 8785 form, except where the case says otherwise.

ceiling.case: build is given the served burnIntentExpirationHeight and the source wallet's withdrawalDelay, each a decimal string below 2^256, and writes maxBlockHeight, their ceiling, into the request; complete refuses a signed burn intent whose maxBlockHeight is not that value read as a decimal. good is the choice's inputs for M5's burn intent, whose maxBlockHeight is 39350204; each refusal changes one member of good, or of M5's burn intent; sourceNetworkChanged builds with another sourceNetwork than the one M5's credential names.

built.case: a 12-second chain's 7 days, 50400 blocks: 100 s is 8.33 blocks, rounded up to 9
a delay of 604800 blocks: 100 blocks exactly

buildRefusals.case: sourceNetwork absent: no network the height was read for
burnIntentExpirationHeight a JSON number, where /v1/info serves a string
a ceiling above 2^256 - 1: height 2^256 - 1 and a delay of 1, whose margin is 1

sourceNetworkChanged.case: the choice's height read for eip155:84532, and M5's burn intent, signed to spend on eip155:5042002, given to complete

completeRefusals.case: the stock client's own maxBlockHeight, 2^256 - 1, an intent that never lapses: createBurnIntent's output with its salt set to M5's
